evidence: app/src/app/shared/card-list.ts:14 — CardList drops types from cards and takes no per-item content
app/src/app/pages/home/home.html:36 — home hand-rolls its own card-grid because CardList can't show types/pagination

abstraction_design.rationale: CardList stopped one step short of the real variation (types on cards, per-item extras), so two pages copy its markup; the rest of the abstractions (MoveTable, toCards, TypeBadge, resolver factory) stretch without flags.

findings.issue: CardList omits card types and per-item extras, so home (home.html:36-40) and team (team-page.ts:25-35) duplicate the card-grid loop; any card markup or ordering change touches three templates.
findings.suggestion: Extend CardList with a `types` input and projected per-item content (ng-content slot), then use it on home and team.

findings.issue: The team data query string is built identically in the route resolver and in TeamPage.load (team-page.ts:97); the two can drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single helper (e.g. `teamPath(names)` in PageData or TeamStore) used by both.

findings.issue: The page-data path format is an implicit string contract shared between route resolvers (app.routes.ts:28-35) and the loadPageData switch; renaming a path key means editing two files with no compile-time check.
findings.suggestion: Introduce typed path builders next to the VM models so both sides reference the same constants.

findings.issue: The default API base URL 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated here and in server/api-client.ts:13.
findings.suggestion: Keep the default in one module and import it into both.

findings.issue: Caching policy (TTL, eviction) is split across the server cache here and the client cache in page-data.ts:13-28, plus per-page TransferState; a caching-rule change touches all three.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared TTL/cache option constant (or a small cache helper) both caches read from.

findings.issue: The type color convention (`var(--type-<name>)`) is re-implemented inline instead of reusing TypeBadge (type-badge.ts:16).
findings.suggestion: Use TypeBadge with link=true (maybe with a `tile` styling input) for the type list.

findings.issue: Home re-derives type labels client-side (typeRef at home.ts:97-99), duplicating label logic the loaders already own (loaders.ts:135-139), because HomeEntry carries raw type names.
findings.suggestion: Have loadHome emit NamedRefs for types so label resolution stays in the data layer.

findings.issue: Scroll policy is embedded in the root App constructor via a manual router-events subscription and URL diffing; it's the app component's most fragile logic.
findings.suggestion: Move it to a dedicated scrolling service or router feature so the root component stays purely layout.

summary: A consistent page→VM architecture (route resolver → server loader or /_data fetch → typed input) makes most fixes land in one obvious place, and the shared PokemonCard/formatting helpers are genuinely single-sourced. The main editability drag is that CardList never absorbed the app's real card variations, so home and team duplicate the card-grid markup, and a couple of string contracts (team query, page-data paths) live on both sides of the server/client seam. Overall this is easy code to change, with a few known spots to tidy before they compound.
